questions.q: What defines a sequential approval chain in Flow Designer?
options: A later Approval action sits inside the approved branch of an If/Else checking the prior stage's outcome, so it never runs until that stage is approved
All approvers see the request on their list at the same moment, with no particular order
Sequential approvals cannot be built in Flow Designer at all
Every approver must reject the request before it is considered complete
questions.explain: Sequential staging is built by placing the next Approval action downstream of an If/Else that gates on the previous stage's approved outcome.

questions.q: In a parallel approval stage configured as "any," when does the stage resolve?
options: Only after every named approver has responded
As soon as the first response — approve or reject — comes back from any of the named approvers
It never resolves until a manager manually closes it
Only when all approvers reject at the same time
questions.explain: "Any" resolves on the first response; the rest of the group's pending requests become irrelevant once that happens.

questions.q: How does the flow actually find out whether an Approval action was approved or rejected?
options: It cannot — a developer must query the database directly
The approver sends a separate notification manually
The Approval action produces an outcome as a data pill, which an If/Else step then branches on
The flow guesses based on how long the approval took
questions.explain: The outcome is exposed as a pill like any other action output, and a standard If/Else reads it to decide the next step.

questions.q: In the lesson's high-cost equipment example, why is Manager-then-Finance built as sequential rather than parallel?
options: Because Flow Designer does not support parallel approvals for equipment requests
Because Finance shouldn't be asked to review a request Manager hasn't cleared yet — one approval is a real prerequisite for the next
Because sequential approvals are always faster than parallel ones
Because the catalog item's variables require it technically
questions.explain: Sequential staging fits whenever a later approver's review is genuinely contingent on an earlier approver's decision.

questions.q: What typically happens to an "all" parallel approval stage if even one named approver rejects?
options: The stage is unaffected and continues waiting for the remaining approvers
The stage automatically resolves as approved regardless
The stage generally resolves as rejected, since not every approver signed off
Flow Designer deletes the Approval action entirely
questions.explain: "All" requires every named approver to approve; a single rejection among the group typically ends the stage as rejected.
